svg.title: Mixing lowers the Gibbs energy, and the tangent gives the potentials of the members
svg.desc: Left: the Gibbs energy per mole of an ideal binary solid solution of A and B, below the straight line of the two pure end members; the tangent at the composition x* meets x = 0 and x = 1 at the chemical potentials of A and B. Right: the presence test: the plane of the potentials the rest of the system imposes, against three curves of a solid solution; above it the phase is absent, touching it present, dipping below it the phase would lower the Gibbs energy and must form.

g.text: Why a solid solution exists, and what fixes its members
